section: 6.3. An estimate for the plateau question of [IMP26, §3.3]: is $w\in D_7$?

text: Dense (as now). One Howell form $M\times M$ in uint32 is 12.5 GB, twice that with the row pool. The operation count is $\sim M^3/3\approx6\cdot10^{13}$ per pass. On one core (~$10^9$ operations/s in our C) that is 15–20 hours. But $J_7$ is generated not by $M$ but by $\sim\sum_r\sum_{t\le6-\operatorname{ord}r}(t+1)6^t$ rows: about $5\cdot10^4$ per relation with a linear part, that is, of the order of $10^6$ rows, and the closure needs several such passes. In total $10^{14}$–$10^{15}$ operations: days on the test machine, and at the limit of its memory (61 GB, shared with CI). Not recommended.

text: The right measure of the number of columns is the minimal number of generators of $A_n^+/J_n$, that is $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}A_n^+/(J_n+2A_n^+)=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}/\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}^n$. Any monomial basis of $\mathbb Z[G]/\Delta^n$, standard monomials included, has at least that many monomials. magnus_pres.py now prints it as generators ($M_n$ minus the rank of the Howell rows modulo $p$; it does not depend on $E$).

text: Exactness for the infinite $G$. $A_n^+/J_n\cong\mathbb Z^{r}\oplus T$, $T$ a finite 2-group with invariants $2^{v_i}$, so index_logp at modulus $2^E$ is $\sum_i\min(v_i,E)+Er$. The rank $r$ is known exactly: by Quillen's theorem $\mathrm{gr}\,\mathbb Q[G]\cong U(\mathrm{gr}\,G\otimes\mathbb Q)$, so $r_n$ is the sum of the coefficients at $t^1..t^{n-1}$ of $\prod_i(1-t^i)^{-h_i}$ with the torsion-free ranks $h=(2,1,2,0)$: $r_n=2,6,14,27,47,78$ for $n=2..7$; for $n\le6$ it equals the number of columns without a pivot in B. If $\mathrm{index}(E_2)-\mathrm{index}(E_1)=r(E_2-E_1)$, then every $v_i\le E_1$, and for an element of finite order (its image is torsion) membership modulo $2^{E_2}$, $E_2>E_1$, is exact.
